record.paper_title: Properly Coloured Cycles and Paths: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Among all graph gadgets G_x associated with a vertex x and its incident colour set χ(x), where G_x must satisfy properties P1-P4 so that it can serve as a P-gadget in the authors' reduction from properly coloured subgraph problems to perfect matching problems, determine whether the XP-gadget always has the minimum possible numbers of vertices and edges for every value z = |χ(x)| ≥ 2.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.1. The XP-gadget has the minimum number of vertices and edges among all possible P-gadgets for every z ≥ 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let H be an edge-coloured (multi)graph and let χ(x) denote the set of colours appearing on edges incident to a vertex x of H. A walk/subgraph of H is called properly coloured if every two consecutive edges receive different colours. A standard reduction from "properly coloured subgraph" problems to "perfect matching" problems proceeds by replacing each vertex x of H with a graph gadget G_x = G_x(χ(x)) attached to the edges incident to x; the colours in χ(x) are in bijection with designated "ports" of G_x. Call G_x a P-gadget if it satisfies the following four properties:

(P1) G_x is a finite simple graph with a distinguished set of |χ(x)| port-vertices, one for each colour c ∈ χ(x).
(P2) For any two distinct colours a, b ∈ χ(x), the subgraph obtained from G_x by deleting the ports corresponding to a and b admits a perfect matching.
(P3) For every single colour c ∈ χ(x), the subgraph obtained from G_x by deleting the port corresponding to c does not admit a perfect matching.
(P4) The whole graph G_x does not admit a perfect matching.

(These properties guarantee that, when the gadgets G_x are plugged into the reduction, perfect matchings of the resulting graph correspond exactly to choices, at each vertex x, of an unordered pair of distinct colours from χ(x) — which encodes a properly coloured pair of edges meeting at x.)

One explicit construction satisfying (P1)–(P4), called here the XP-gadget, is defined as follows. For z := |χ(x)| ≥ 2, take z port-vertices p_1, …, p_z and a "cross" of internal vertices, and join them so that the resulting graph has the minimum number of internal vertices and edges that the authors of this construction could achieve while still satisfying (P1)–(P4).

Problem. Prove or disprove: for every integer z ≥ 2, among all P-gadgets G_x with |χ(x)| = z (i.e. all finite simple graphs with z designated port-vertices satisfying (P1)–(P4)), the XP-gadget simultaneously minimises the number of vertices and the number of edges.
artifact.status_search_result: The statement is posed as a conjecture about optimality of an explicit gadget construction in a reduction from properly coloured subgraph problems to perfect matching problems. A web search returned no resolution of this specific optimality question; related literature focuses on properly coloured Hamiltonian cycles/paths (e.g., Bollobás–Erdős type problems) and not on minimum-size P-gadgets. No source confirming a proof or disproof was found.

status_evidence.title: Properly coloured Hamiltonian paths in edge-coloured complete graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of properly coloured cycles/paths results; no resolution of the XP-gadget minimality conjecture is mentioned.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the gadget-minimality question is reported in nearby literature.

status_evidence.title: Discrete Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science (PC cycles survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey-style article on properly coloured cycles and paths; the optimality of the XP-gadget appears as an open conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The XP-gadget optimality is stated as a conjecture rather than a theorem.
